facts.statement: Express describes itself as a minimalist web framework for Node.js.
facts.limitations: This is the project description. No performance comparison was tested.

facts.statement: The README registers a GET handler for / that sends Hello World.
facts.limitations: Only the documented root route is depicted.

facts.statement: The README example calls app.listen on port 3000.
facts.limitations: The example was read from source and was not executed.

brief.audience: Developers who have seen a browser request and are new to server routing
brief.objective: Trace one documented request from the root path to a response.

useCase.who: A developer building a first Node.js HTTP example
useCase.situation: The developer wants a root path that returns a greeting
useCase.value: The handler makes the example request and response explicit

brief.styleDirection: Illustrate the request, route match and response as three legible cards. Keep the example snippet legible on a phone.

concepts.premise: Follow one request to the greeting.
concepts.opening: Where does Hello World come from?
concepts.rationale: A single request clarifies the role of the path and handler.

concepts.premise: Read the minimal example line by line.
concepts.opening: This is the line that answers the browser.
concepts.rationale: Code annotations offer a compact walkthrough for a developer.

script.narration: The Express README starts a Node.js example server on port three thousand. We will follow one request to see where its answer comes from.
script.caption: One request to the example server

script.narration: Send a GET request to the root path. In this example the matching line registers a handler for GET and slash.
script.caption: GET / reaches the registered handler

script.narration: The handler calls response dot send with Hello World. That string is the example response. The animation traces the documented code.
script.caption: The handler sends Hello World

storyboard.visual: Show a browser card next to a server card labeled localhost:3000.
storyboard.animation: Emphasize the port and slide a request card toward the server.

storyboard.visual: Place a GET / card next to the app.get line.
storyboard.animation: Match the HTTP method and route path with a simple highlight.

storyboard.visual: Show res.send beside a Hello World response card.
storyboard.animation: Move the response card back to the browser and hold.
